We're finalizing our on-prem deployment requirements and want to validate a few items around BYOK, local key wrapping (we call it "local-wrapflow"), and what telemetry/evidence you can expose for audits. Attached are our initial requirements and a simple network diagram. High level asks: 

- Can Redwood run with a customer-managed HSM in our VPC (FIPS 140-2 L3 preferred) while allowing Redwood to perform runtime key wrapping/unwrap for ephemeral tokens?
- What telemetry/forensics will you provide for key access and operator actions (audit logs, immutability, retention)?
- How does key rotation work when we own the root (BYOK)? We want a zero-downtime rotation plan and clear rollback criteria.

We're targeting a compliance review window the week of Apr 12 and procurement needs a high-level SOW & evidence list for our legal team. Can you confirm who from Redwoodops will own the operator-facing runbook?

Thanks,

Samir — thanks for the clear summary and the diagrams. Quick answers up front, then a short plan: 

1) HSM in-customer-VPC: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-provisioned HSMs (we commonly validate YubiHSM/Thales/Entrust appliances) connected over cross-account peering or private link. We run the inference runtime in your VPC subnet(s) and call the HSM for wrap/unwrap via a dedicated gateway.

2) Local-wrapflow: We support a "wrap-as-a-service" model where your root key never leaves the HSM. Redwood generates ephemeral wrapping keys inside the HSM and stores only wrapped blobs. Operator processes can never extract raw root key material. We will provide a sequence diagram and an operator runbook draft — attaching the runbook draft.

3) Telemetry & evidence: We expose an immutable audit stream for all HSM operations (wrap/unwrap/sign/get-key-metadata) with HSM-signed timestamps where available. Logs are pushed to your logging endpoint (S3/GCS/ELK) and we can generate a per-rotation evidence bundle (signed certificates + operation list). Retention configurable by policy.

Rotation model (short):
- You rotate root in HSM (either in-place or via new HSM).
- Redwood performs an atomic rewrap of active key blobs (ephemeral keys) using the new root; this is a streaming operation with per-shard progress and automated fallback to previous root for 24h.
- Automated health checks validate token re-issuance and KV cache consistency.

Next steps proposal:
- Architecture call (30m) this Thu Apr 1 to walk the sequence diagram and ops playbook.
- We'll deliver a short evidence checklist for your legal/procurement by Apr 2.
- Follow-up: a dry-run cutover plan (non-prod) with operator checklist.

I copied Vanessa (Network + Ops guardrails) and Hannah (Cutover and ceremony rehearsals) to coordinate. Attaching operator-runbook-draft.md and a high-level sequence diagram link.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Quick ops notes from the network/egress side: 

- Network paths: we'll want a dedicated subnet for Redwood runtime with strict egress routes to the HSM gateway. No public internet egress from that subnet except for patching windows (behind your proxy).
- Operator separation: operator consoles must live in a separate management VPC with MFA + bastion. We'll use short-lived certificates for operator sessions — no static operator keys.
- Fail-open vs fail-closed: default is fail-closed for unwrap operations. We can provide an emergency escape hatch (manual unwrap with quorum via operator witness) but that requires an agreed SOP and an escrow key held by your security team.

I also flagged the retention and immutability requirements with our infra team — we will provide a draft retention policy for audit review.

Vanessa Ortiz
Network Security Lead, Redwood Inference
